summary: The root شطأ primarily refers to the shoot or sprout that emerges from a seed or plant, especially a grain. It signifies the initial growth or offshoot, like a young branch or sucker.

headwords.def: : see 4. Also He walked on the شَاطِئ, i. e. bank, or side, of the river. (K, * TA.) And He cut lengthwise [ into slices, or strips, ] the hump of a camel, and a skin, or hide. (TA.) He subdued, overcame, overpowered, or mastered, a man. (K.) He compressed his wife. (K.) [And سَطَأَ and طَشَأَ signify the same.] شَطَأَالنَّاقَةَ, (AA, S, K,) aor. شَطَاَ [as in other senses], (TA,) inf. n. شَطْءٌ, (AA, S,) He bound the saddle upon the she-camel.
inf. n. تَشْطِىْءٌ, It (a valley) had its two sides ( شَاطِئَاهُ, TA) flowing [ with water ]. (IAar, K.)
I walked upon one شَاطِئ [i. e. bank, or side, of a river or valley, ] while he walked upon the other شاطئ. (S, K. *)

; (S, Msb;) or, aor. شَطَاَ, inf. n. شَطْءٌ and شُطُوْءٌ; (K;) or both; (TA;) It put forth its شَطْء [or sprouts, &c.]; (S, K;) syn. فَرَّخَ; (Msb;) said of seed-produce; (S, Msb, K;) and in like manner said of palm-trees ( نَخْل ); and the former verb, said of trees ( شَجَر ), they put forth sprouts around their bases, or stems. (K.) And اشطأت الشَّجَرَةُ بِغُصُونِهَا The tree put forth its branches.
Q. Q. 1 شَطْيَأَ , (K, TA,) said of a man, (TA,) i. q. رَهْيَأَ, (K, TA,) meaning He was weak (TA) in his opinion, or judgment, (K, TA,) and in his affair. (TA.)

(S, Msb, K, &c.) and (TA as from the K [but not in the CK nor in my MS. copy of the K, though a known dial. var. of the former as will be shown in what follows,]) The فِرَاخ [or sprouts ] of seed-produce, (IAar, S, Msb, K,) and of plants, or herbage, (S,) and of palm-trees: or the leaves thereof; (K. TA;) i. e. of seed-produce: (TA:) and the shoots that come forth (Msb, K) from, (Msb,) or around, (K,) the bases, or stems, (Msb, K,) of plants, or herbage, (Msb,) or of trees: (K:) pl.
: see the next preceding paragraph, in two places.

[app. a n. un. of شَطْءٌ, q. v. Also] A green palm-branch: one says, لَهَا قَدٌّ كَالشَّطْأَةِ She has a figure like the green palm-branch. (A, TA.) And A slice, or strip, i. e. a piece cut lengthwise, of a camel's hump, and of a skin, or hide. (A, TA.)

(S, Msb, K) and (K) The bank, or side, ( شَطّ, S, K, and جَانِب, S, Msb,) of a valley (S, Msb, K) and of a river: (K:) and some say that the former signifies the extremity, or edge, or side, ( طَرَف,) of a river; and the shore of the sea: the pl. of the latter is شُطُوْءٌ; and of the former, شَوَاطِئُ and شُطْآنٌ; (K, TA;) or this last, as is said in the M, may be pl. of شَطْءٌ. (TA.) Accord.

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
mentions_note: Forms Lane discusses inside another entry rather than defining as a headword. Values index into headwords[].
